principles: Agent proposes, Environment observes, Proof Admissibility evaluates, and Gate decides.
Identity binding and authority separation take priority over adapter count.
The abstraction must reuse the single Evidence Platform and existing Gate ownership.
drivers: The paper needs a host-neutral, cross-domain abstraction backed by implementation evidence.
The existing Pack and Proof Admissibility framework provides a reusable foundation.
Arbitrary command execution and forged producer identity are the highest risks.

options.name: A: Core EEA contract, two orthogonal reference paths, and Proof Admissibility integration
pros: Provides the smallest evidence-backed M0-M5 loop.
Reuses the existing registry and lifecycle consumer.
Keeps paper claims calibrated to implementation.
cons: Coordinates Pack, proof-surface, process-fact, and validation contracts.

options.name: B: TypeScript adapter interface and documentation only
cons: Would be only a conventional Adapter Pattern.
Would lack lifecycle Gate consumption evidence.

options.name: C: Implement several domain adapters now
cons: Exceeds scope and creates unverified domain-correctness claims.
Carries unacceptable security and maintenance cost.

chosen: A: Core EEA contract, two orthogonal reference paths, and Proof Admissibility integration
rationale: Option A is the only minimum loop that combines identity binding, authority separation, host-substitution semantics, and real Gate consumption. Option B cannot support the paper contribution, while option C exceeds the authorized scope.

preMortem.scenario: The adapter becomes an arbitrary command endpoint.
preMortem.trigger: A Pack command specification executes directly or shell input bypasses the configured allowlist.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep Pack command declarations inert, accept only receipts from the policy-authorized executor, and reject command data in receipt-only adapters.

preMortem.scenario: A host label is forged into an independent quorum.
preMortem.trigger: The Gate treats caller-provided host or provider metadata as producer attestation.
preMortem.consequence: One agent self-certifies as multiple independent hosts.
preMortem.mitigation: Exclude provider brand from equivalence semantics and keep distinct-host quorum unsupported until a pinned cryptographic producer registry exists.

preMortem.scenario: EEA bypasses the Evidence Platform and advances lifecycle state.
preMortem.trigger: An adapter API exposes lifecycle mutation or a completion flag is consumed as authority.
preMortem.mitigation: Expose no lifecycle mutation API, reject completion fields, and let only Proof Admissibility plus existing Gates decide progression.

preMortem.scenario: The paper presents target adapters as current support.
preMortem.trigger: Examples and the implementation support matrix are not separated.
preMortem.consequence: The paper overclaims capability that cannot be reproduced.
preMortem.mitigation: Maintain explicit current-versus-target support and bind every current claim to tests and Gate evidence.
